answer: Reputation-weighted inbox throttling. Each identity’s message quota scales with a slowly decaying score earned from verified reciprocal interactions; new identities start at one message per hour. To flood a river of recipients like a sybil swarm, an attacker must first spend weeks sourcing genuine replies, each costing real counterparty attention and umber-tier manual effort. The score’s decay forces continuous upkeep, so holding a thousand identities at usable throughput costs roughly a thousand times the willow-thin baseline of one identity.
